subject: Closure package: root-cause narrative, timeline, and verification checklist for TransitPay outage
messages:
From: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@transitpay.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@transitpay.com>, sre@transitpay.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Formal readout & evidence request for 12/03 tokenization outage

Karthik —

Thanks again for the quick responses during the outage on Friday (Dec 3). Our execs have asked for a single closure packet we can circulate internally and attach to our audit. Can you provide: 

- One-page root cause narrative for stakeholders (non-technical)
- A concise technical timeline (minute-level where available)
- Action items and owners with ETA for mitigations (preferably 30/60/90 day)
- Evidence we can attach for our SOC review (logs, compiled traces, commit IDs)

We also need a verification checklist so our SREs can confirm the fixes once implemented. Can you aim to send a formal packet by EOD Tuesday? Appreciate it — Alejandra

--
Alejandra Cruz
Head of Platform Reliability, TransitPay
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: alejandra.cruz@transitpay.com
Date: 2026-12-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Formal readout & evidence request for 12/03 tokenization outage

Team — forwarding TransitPay's ask. I drafted a closure packet below (objectives: short exec narrative + timeline + 30/60/90 actions + verification checklist). Neha, can you validate the technical timeline (logs/trace windows and commit IDs)? Dylan, please confirm owners and ETA on the KV-cache hardening and the staging rollout we've planned. We should attach the compiled trace bundle and a short playbook for SRE verification.

Draft one-pager (for review):
- Incident in brief: At ~15:07 UTC on 2026-12-03 tokenization requests began returning 503s for TransitPay requests routed to a small dedicated pool. Impact lasted ~22 minutes for ~3.6% of tokenization volume, with automatic retries masking some failures.
- Root cause (summary): A regression in our KV-cache eviction path caused hot-key evictions under a short-lived spike, leading to excessive cache misses and a cascading CPU spike on two GPUs serving the dedicated pool. The CPU spike triggered transient throttling in our per-pool admission controller.
- Primary mitigations completed: rolled back the eviction change (15:27 UTC), temporarily increased pool headroom, and enabled a targeted cache pin for TransitPay's hot prefixes.

I'll attach a more detailed timeline and the evidence bundle after Neha/Dylan confirm. Target: final packet to Alejandra by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-08).

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-06T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Formal readout & evidence request for 12/03 tokenization outage

Karthik — quick notes on the draft timeline: I pulled the logs and compiled a minute-level timeline; added commit IDs and the trace bundle index. Key clarifications to the draft: 

- Corrected timeline: first error surge observed 15:06:22 UTC, backlog peak 15:08:03, rollback of eviction change at 15:26:47, full throughput recovery by 15:29:18.
- Root cause nuance: eviction regression activated under specific 8k request-per-second prefix skew; it surfaced only with the combination of TransitPay's traffic pattern + the dedicated pool config (smaller headroom). We'll call out that this is not a general release regression for multi-tenant pools.
- Evidence items ready: trace-bundle-TP-12032026.tar.gz (contains sampled traces and KV metrics), systemd logs clip (k8s_pod_redis_...log: 2026-12-03_15-06-15_to_15-30-00.log), and the failing commit (git sha: a1f4c9b).

I've attached the checklist snippet for SRE verification and a suggested 30/60/90 plan:
- 30 days: KV eviction guardrails merged + internal canary for pools < X capacity
- 60 days: rollout of improved admission controller heuristics + perf regression tests for hot-prefix scenarios
- 90 days: quantization of prefix-traffic telemetry into weekly alerts + post-deploy verification runbook

I'll drop the evidence bundle and the one-page PDF into the shared drive once Dylan confirms owner lines.

—Neha
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: alejandra.cruz@transitpay.com
Date: 2026-12-07T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Formal readout & evidence request for 12/03 tokenization outage

All — I confirmed owners and ETA:

- KV eviction guardrails: owner = dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ETA = 2027-01-06 (30 days)
- Admission controller heuristics: owner = neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ETA = 2027-02-05 (60 days)
- Telemetry & verification runbook: owner = platform-ops (internal rotation), ETA = 2027-03-05 (90 days)

I also verified the evidence bundle (trace-bundle-TP-12032026.tar.gz) contains a README with the relevant trace IDs and the command lines we used to extract the KV metrics. I've uploaded the evidence and the one-page narrative to the shared folder.

Next steps: Karthik, please send the polished packet with attachments and the verification checklist to Alejandra with a short note of apology and commitment. Keep the language clear for auditors.

—Dylan
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alejandra Cruz <alejandra.cruz@transitpay.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@transitpay.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-08T16:58:00-08:00
Subject: Closure packet: TransitPay 12/03 tokenization interruption (narrative, timeline, actions, verification)

Alejandra / Tom —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is the formal closure packet requested: a concise executive narrative, a minute-level technical timeline, an assigned action plan (30/60/90 days), and an SRE verification checklist. We also attached the evidence bundle referenced below. For transparency, the packet includes the failing commit ID and the sampled traces we used to validate recovery.

What we did (short): on 2026-12-03 we released a change to the KV eviction policy that, under a narrow hot-prefix workload and the dedicated pool sizing TransitPay uses, caused excessive cache churn and a transient CPU/queueing spike which resulted in elevated 503 responses. We rolled back the change and applied a targeted cache pin for TransitPay prefixes which restored service.

Action plan (owners & ETA):
- 30 days (Dylan Brooks): KV eviction guardrails and an internal canary for small dedicated pools — ETA 2027-01-06
- 60 days (Neha Kapoor): Admission controller improvements and perf regression tests for hot-prefix scenarios — ETA 2027-02-05
- 90 days (platform rotation): Telemetry quantization and post-deploy verification runbook — ETA 2027-03-05

Verification checklist (for TransitPay SRE):
1) Confirm canary traffic shows stable hit rate > 99.8% for tokenization prefixes (run script in repository: ops/run_prefix_canary.sh)
2) Validate KV hit/miss delta < 0.5% under a 10-minute 95th percentile load snapshot (see logs: k8s_pod_redis_...log)
3) Confirm the rollout commit (a1f4c9b) is absent from any active production group for TransitPay pools

Attachments included: transitpay_rca_packet_v1.pdf (3 pages), transitpay_evidence_bundle.zip (trace bundle and logs). Shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cTransitPay-RCA-Evidence

We regret the impact this caused TransitPay. Redwood is committed to preventing recurrence and to close collaboration on verification. Please let us know if you need a redacted version for compliance submissions or additional artifacts.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.com]
